record.title: Physical touch reaches gestures and visible controls
record.method: UART contact counts, owner interaction, native screenshots and full post-run storage checks
record.observation: The N45AP physical route supports unlock, Settings taps, visible pinch enlargement and brightness adjustment. The accepted finger-identity trial submitted 439 frames, including 123 with two active contacts, and completed a clean reboot.
record.limits: The earlier 1,476-frame run proves two-contact delivery but did not establish visible pinch. The later owner-confirmed gesture is separate acceptance. One offline Photos fixture is not general gesture or app coverage. The headless QEMU tree disables touch; its passing boot is not touch evidence.

excerpts.content:
The physical interactive window lasted about 12 minutes after client attach.
The user reported that the tests performed worked, but could not establish
visible pinch-to-zoom. UART recorded 1,476 submitted frames: 488 contained
two contact records and 470 had two simultaneously active IDs. The median
interval within contact sequences was 46 ms; delays ranged from 45 to 247 ms
when intervals of 250 ms or more were excluded. This proves two-contact
delivery and real timing, not visual acceptance of a pinch gesture.
The saved SpringBoard preferences retain `SBAutoLockTime = -1` and
`SBAutoDimTime = -1` before and after the run.

The clean UART reboot was requested at 780 seconds and Jumpdrive returned
at about 800 seconds, with no panic, full queue or failed-request marker.
The post-run 512 MiB data copy has SHA-256
`5232beedca22b3211dc847011e3926fea974addbad9889086557104ce918d47a`,
the clean bit set and `fsck_hfs -dfn` exit 0. The root hash is unchanged.
Jumpdrive reported 37% battery before and after, charging on laptop USB.

[…]

Physical trial 18 used the finger-identity revision alongside the brightness
minimum adjustment. The user confirmed that spreading two fingers enlarged
the grid in Photos. Before clean shutdown, UART recorded 439 submitted
frames including 123 with two active contacts. This is visible pinch
acceptance, beyond packet-count evidence. All 30 CTests and 447 Python tests
pass; the private input image fits at 27,272 of 27,648 bytes. The combined
headless QEMU build also completed a clean reboot. The full 512 MiB post-run data copy matched the UART SHA-256
`da79d8ea036df8039e45c28400d5cf82dc3c77de1ac19fbff1f857aac0b85ff7`,
retained the clean data bit and passed fsck. The root hash remained unchanged.
excerpts.note: Exact selected notebook lines at the reviewed revision. Ellipses mark omitted passages.

excerpts.content:
The brightness revision maps the slider to the device-tree visible minimum
while retaining complete blanking. QEMU verified original brightness writes
and a clean reboot. The touch revision assigns distinct stable finger
identities, fixing a collision in the original HID child-event table.
All 30 CTests and 447 Python tests pass. The combined build passed a QEMU
boot and clean reboot, but its headless tree disables Z2; a separate SPI2
tree repeats an early null abort. Physical trial 18 received explicit user confirmation of the visible minimum,
Power blank/wake and pinch enlargement. It completed a clean UART reboot;
the full data copy matched its UART hash, retained the clean bit, passed
fsck and confirmed an unchanged root. Automatic extraction recovered six
valid screenshots, including two from that trial. No PMIC configuration,
CPU clock or root-volume change was made.
